title: Trump dismisses concerns over AI dangers
summary: The US president said calls to slow down AI development are a "sick conspiracy," claiming that they only serve China. Market leaders have warned of the dangers of the technology's development pace.

image.caption: US President Trump believes he is capable of holding AI development at bay.Image: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has rebuffed criticism of AI technology progressing too quickly, calling it a "SICK conspiracy."

This comes despite calls by market leaders such as Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman for more governmental regulation on AI. In recent months, several incidents have highlighted the risk of AI agents going rogue and carrying out a series of hacks.
"The only control or ‘guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump posted on his Truth Social account.

blocks.caption: Anthropic is the developer of popular AI module ClaudeImage: IMAGO/ZUMA Press

blocks.text: According to Trump, his administration has already prevented Anthropic from "doing bad, or potentially bad" things with their technology.
The Pentagon previously tried to brand Anthropic's models a security risk and posed a temporary ban on one of its more advanced models.
"There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China," Trump wrote.

Anthropic boss Amodei warned against uncontrolled global AI development over the weekend saying that there's a risk of AI-led agents taking over the entire internet within six to 12 months. Microsoft published its own code of conduct to ensure human control over AI.
This led to AI stocks falling worldwide, including those of chip maker Nvidia (3.5%) and Elon Musk's SpaceX (1.7%).
What is AI's biggest risk: Speed or autonomy?
